name: bulk_create
description:
Create multiple entities in one call for performance.

Each element may be written either nested or flat:
    {"type": "line", "params": {"start": [0,0], "end": [10,0]}}
    {"type": "line", "start": [0,0], "end": [10,0]}
Both are accepted, and a mixture is accepted too - keys inside "params" win
over keys of the same name at the top level. Common alternative names are
resolved as well (start_point/point1/from, center_point, vertices/pts,
insertion_point, contents/value, pattern_name).

Supported types: line, circle, arc, polyline, rectangle, text, mtext,
ellipse, hatch.

Every element that does not become an entity is returned in "skipped" with
its index, its type and the reason, so a count of 0 always says why.
summary: Create multiple entities in one call for performance.

name: bulk_erase

Erase multiple entities at once. By handles list, or by layer/type filter.

Destructive — pass __confirm=true to proceed.
summary: Erase multiple entities at once. By handles list, or by layer/type filter.

name: cancel_command
description:
Send ESC to AutoCAD to abort a command that is waiting at a prompt.

A command sitting at a prompt still lets the bridge answer, but it eats
whatever is sent next as its prompt response, so a stuck prompt has to be
cleared before anything else works.

This cannot close a modal dialog: a dialog runs its own message loop and only
a human can dismiss it. When CMDACTIVE reports a dialog the call refuses and
says so rather than pretending to have helped.

repeat  1..5 ESC pairs; a few commands (MATCHPROP is the usual offender)
        re-arm themselves after a single ESC.

The cancel is queued, so the state in the reply is the state *before* it -
call system_status again to confirm the command line is idle. Sending ESC
modifies nothing, so this tool stays available in read-only mode: it is what
unsticks a prompt when everything else is refused.
summary: Send ESC to AutoCAD to abort a command that is waiting at a prompt.

name: capture_screenshot
description:
Capture the AutoCAD window as PNG or JPEG and save it. Returns the file path,
so the image can be viewed to verify that an operation did what was intended.

area       "window" (default) grabs the whole application frame; "drawing"
           crops to the drawing area alone, typically a third of the pixels.
max_width  Downscale to this width, default 1600 px; 0 keeps full size.
format     "png" (default) or "jpeg" ("jpg" is accepted too) - for a CAD
           screen JPEG is roughly a tenth of the bytes.
quality    JPEG quality, default 85, clamped to 20..100.

The answer reports area_used, the captured size, whether it was scaled, and the
format actually written - which falls back to PNG on a runtime with no JPEG
encoder - so the caller always knows what it got.
summary: Capture the AutoCAD window as PNG or JPEG and save it.

name: execute_command
description:
Execute a raw AutoCAD command, optionally with all of its interactive inputs.

The command and every item of `inputs` are joined into ONE space-separated
string and sent to AutoCAD in a single call. Interactive / multi-step
commands MUST be passed this way (command + all prompt responses together);
splitting them across several execute_command calls does not work, because
AutoCAD cancels a command that is still awaiting input when the next string
is queued.

The command runs asynchronously, so the send itself cannot report success. The
reply carries a `since` marker; pass it to `read_command_line` to see what
AutoCAD actually did with the string.

Examples:
    execute_command("ZOOM E")
    execute_command("_.CIRCLE", ["100,100", "40"])
    execute_command("_.POLYGON", ["6", "400,250", "_I", "60"])

Two refusals protect the bridge, both overridable with force=true: the call
is refused while the command line is busy (anything sent then is eaten as a
prompt response - call cancel_command first), and it is refused for commands
that raise a modal dialog before they are even sent, naming a dialog-free
alternative where one exists. The command name is prefixed with _ by default so a localised
AutoCAD accepts it; never with _. , which would force the built-in definition
and break a command redefined by LISP or ARX.
summary: Execute a raw AutoCAD command, optionally with all of its interactive inputs.

name: plot_devices
description:
List plot devices, plot style tables, and a device's paper sizes in mm.

Canonical paper names are not guessable - the A1 sheet a localized AutoCAD
shows as "ISO A1 (841.00 x 594.00 mm)" is called
"ISO_full_bleed_A1_(841.00_x_594.00_MM)" in the API. Pass `device` (e.g.
"DWG To PDF.pc3") to get its media list with sheet size, printable area and
margins in millimetres, so plot_to_pdf(paper=...) can be given a name that
exists. `filter` narrows the media list by substring, e.g. "A1".

`plotter` is an accepted synonym for `device`. Some MCP hosts route calls
through a bridge that reserves the argument name "device" for itself and
consumes it before the tool ever sees it; on those hosts `device` silently
arrives empty and `plotter` is the way through. Pass one or the other -
`device` wins if both are given.

Called with no device, it lists the sheets of "DWG To PDF.pc3". The answer
always echoes `requested_device` and `requested_filter`, so a dropped
argument is visible rather than silently ignored.
summary: List plot devices, plot style tables, and a device's paper sizes in mm.

name: plot_to_pdf
description:
Plot the drawing to PDF and wait for the file to be written.

Goes through the PlottingServices API rather than the command line, so it
reports the real outcome and the real file size instead of fire-and-forget.

output_path  Where to write. A relative path resolves next to the drawing.
device       Plot device, default "DWG To PDF.pc3". See plot_devices.
plotter      Synonym for `device`, for MCP hosts whose bridge reserves the
             argument name "device" and eats it before the tool sees it.
             `device` wins if both are given.
paper        Canonical or localized media name, or "auto" (default): the
             smallest sheet whose *printable* area fits the window at the
             requested scale, which is what picks full-bleed sheets over
             bordered ones when the frame reaches the paper edge.
style_table  Plot style table, default "monochrome.ctb"; "none" keeps
             whatever the layout already uses.
area         extents | window | display | layout | limits. Defaults to
             "window" when `window` is given, otherwise "extents".
window       [x1, y1, x2, y2] in drawing units - normally the sheet frame,
             which in these drawings is a closed LWPOLYLINE on Defpoints.
scale        "1=1" (default), "1:100", a number, or "fit".
offset       "center" (default) or [dx, dy] in millimetres.
orientation  "auto" (default), "portrait" or "landscape".
layout       Layout to plot; default the current one.
lineweights  Honour lineweights, default True.
overwrite    Replace an existing file, default True.
trim         Crop the finished page down to the plotted window, default
             True. Set False to keep the whole printer sheet.

The result reports the media actually used and its millimetre size.

AutoCAD can only plot onto a paper size the device defines, so a
non-standard sheet (840x594, 297x630) is plotted 1:1 centred on the nearest
larger sheet and the surplus is cropped afterwards, here in the MCP server,
using PdfSharp, and only for a `window` plot at a fixed scale - an `extents`
or `fit` plot has no exact target size to crop to.

The answer always says what happened: `trimmed` true or false, with
`trimmed_size_mm` and `trim_box_mm` when it worked, and `trim_error` or
`trim_reason` when it was not attempted (`trim` false), or `trim_error` with the
text when it was attempted and failed - a page smaller than the target, a
missing file, or a malformed PDF. It is never
swallowed, and a failed crop never invalidates the plot.
summary: Plot the drawing to PDF and wait for the file to be written.

Remove all unused layers, blocks, styles, and linetypes from the drawing.

Destructive — pass __confirm=true to proceed.
summary: Remove all unused layers, blocks, styles, and linetypes from the drawing.

name: read_command_line
description:
Read AutoCAD's recent command activity and the last command-line prompt.

Pass the "since" value returned by execute_command to see exactly what that
call produced: which commands started, ended, failed or were cancelled, plus
the last line AutoCAD echoed (where messages like "Unknown command" appear).
Call with since=0 for the whole recent history.
summary: Read AutoCAD's recent command activity and the last command-line prompt.

name: read_external_dwg
description:

Reads it as a side database and reports layers, blocks, xrefs, layouts and
entity counts. Use this to check a drawing before opening it.
summary: Inspect a DWG file WITHOUT opening it in AutoCAD.

summary: Reload an xref to pick up changes made to the source DWG.

name: select_by_properties
description:
Find entities matching property filters (AND logic).

`type` accepts the .NET name ("BlockReference"), the AutoCAD class name
("AcDbBlockReference"), the DXF name ("INSERT") or an alias ("block",
"text", "anytext", "pline", "dimension", "curve"), and a comma-separated
list of any of those. `block_name` further restricts block references to
one block definition.

`fields` trims each record to the named keys, and `handles_only` returns a
flat list of handles instead of a record per entity - both exist to keep a
large selection from filling the answer with fields the caller will not read.
`fields` takes an array or a comma-separated string, and `handle` is always kept
whether it is listed or not.
summary: Find entities matching property filters (AND logic).

name: select_by_window
description:
Find entities in a rectangular region.

mode="window" (default) returns only entities fully inside the box;
mode="crossing" also returns anything the box touches — use it when picking
a title block or a sheet region, whose entities stick out past the frame.

Optional layer/type filters narrow the result; `type` accepts "INSERT",
"AcDbBlockReference", "BlockReference" or "block" alike. The answer carries
`total` and `truncated` so a cut-off list is never mistaken for a complete one.

Over direct JSON-RPC the plugin accepts either `min_point`/`max_point` or `min`/`max`.
summary: Find entities in a rectangular region.

summary: Set drawing properties, including custom name/value fields used by title blocks.

Change draw order so entities render in front of or behind others.

position: top, bottom, above or below. above/below also need reference_id.
summary: Change draw order so entities render in front of or behind others.

name: set_dynamic_block_property

summary: Set one dynamic block parameter (e.g. a visibility state, length or angle).

summary: Change properties of an existing entity: layer, color (ACI 0-255), linetype, lineweight.

name: set_page_setup

Configure a layout's page setup before plotting.

device: plotter/printer name (see list_plot_devices).
paper_size: canonical media name (see list_paper_sizes).
plot_type: Display, Extents, Limits, View, Window or Layout.
scale: "1:100" style ratio; or set scale_to_fit=true.
rotation: 0, 90, 180 or 270.
summary: Configure a layout's page setup before plotting.

name: set_server_options
description:
Change and persist the safety posture.

read_only=True refuses every drawing-modifying tool (safe inspection mode).
confirm_destructive=True (default) makes erase/delete/purge tools require
__confirm=true. audit_log toggles the JSONL activity log.
summary: Change and persist the safety posture.

name: set_system_variable
description: Set an AutoCAD system variable (e.g., DIMTXT, LTSCALE, OSMODE). Value can be number or string.
summary: Set an AutoCAD system variable (e.g., DIMTXT, LTSCALE, OSMODE). Value can be number or string.

name: set_table_cell
description:
Write table cells.

Either row+column+text for a single cell, or cells as a list of
{"row": r, "column": c, "text": "..."} to update many at once.
summary: Write table cells.

name: set_ucs
description:
Set the active UCS.

Pass name to activate a saved UCS ('World' resets), or origin (+ optional
x_axis/y_axis) to define one, optionally saving it as save_as.
summary: Set the active UCS.

name: set_units
description: Set drawing units. linear_units: 1=Scientific,2=Decimal,3=Engineering,4=Architectural. insert_units: 4=mm,5=cm,6=m.
summary: Set drawing units. linear_units: 1=Scientific,2=Decimal,3=Engineering,4=Architectural. insert_units: 4=mm,5=cm,6=m.

description: Set a viewport's scale, e.g. "1:100". Temporarily unlocks a locked viewport.
summary: Set a viewport's scale, e.g. "1:100". Temporarily unlocks a locked viewport.

name: set_xdata
description:
Attach extended entity data (XData) to an entity under an application name.

Registers the application name automatically. Useful for tagging entities
with your own metadata that survives in the DWG.
summary: Attach extended entity data (XData) to an entity under an application name.

name: set_xref_path
description: Repoint a broken or moved xref at a new file path.
summary: Repoint a broken or moved xref at a new file path.

name: sync_attributes
description:
Add attributes to existing block references that were added to the block
definition after they were inserted (equivalent to ATTSYNC).
summary: Add attributes to existing block references that were added to the block

name: system_status
description:
Get the AutoCAD plugin status, version, and active document info.

Also reports the command-line state read from CMDACTIVE / CMDNAMES:
command_active, command_active_flags, command_names, command_state
(idle | command | dialog | script), dialog_active and script_active, plus
command_hint while something is active and last_command once the plugin has
seen one.

That is what separates the two ways the bridge goes quiet: a command waiting
at a prompt (clear it with cancel_command) from a modal dialog, which stops
Application.Idle entirely and can only be dismissed by hand.
summary: Get the AutoCAD plugin status, version, and active document info.

name: undo_last
description: Undo the last N operations in AutoCAD.
summary: Undo the last N operations in AutoCAD.

name: ungroup
description:
Remove a group definition; its entities stay in the drawing.
Destructive — pass __confirm=true to proceed.
summary: Remove a group definition; its entities stay in the drawing.

name: unload_xref
description: Unload an xref (keeps the attachment, hides the geometry).
summary: Unload an xref (keeps the attachment, hides the geometry).

name: update_dimensions
description:
Regenerate dimensions from current settings, optionally reassigning a style.

Omit ids to update every dimension in the current space.
summary: Regenerate dimensions from current settings, optionally reassigning a style.

name: zoom_extents
description: Zoom to show all entities in the drawing.
summary: Zoom to show all entities in the drawing.

name: zoom_window
description:
Zoom to a specific rectangular area defined by min [x,y] and max [x,y] corners.

Over direct JSON-RPC the plugin accepts either `min`/`max` or `min_point`/`max_point`.
summary: Zoom to a specific rectangular area defined by min [x,y] and max [x,y] corners.
